data.about: Four forces on four different lines: the force diagram still gives the resultant by laying them tip to tail, but there is no longer a single crossing point to place it on. The trial funicular solves that — any pole, any starting point: draw one string per ray between the action lines, and where the FIRST and LAST strings meet is a point on the resultant’s line of action. Drag the pole and the starting point: the funicular changes shape completely, the answer does not move.

steps.caption: EX 1 task 2: four forces, four different lines of action — the resultant needs a TRIAL FUNICULAR to be placed
steps.title: The exercise

steps.caption: left: F₁ … F₄ green on their lines of action — no two of them meet in one common point, so the trick of task 1 is not available
steps.title: The four given forces

steps.caption: right: the four vectors laid tip to tail, each parallel to its own line of action — this already answers HOW BIG and WHICH WAY, but says nothing about WHERE
steps.title: The load line

steps.caption: right: choose a pole — anywhere (drag it!) — and draw the rays from it to every division of the load line: the rays are the “handles” of the funicular
steps.title: Pick any pole o

steps.caption: left: start anywhere on line 1 (drag the start!) and walk: between two action lines draw a string parallel to the ray that separates them — string 1 ∥ ray 1, string 2 ∥ ray 2, and so on to string 4
steps.title: The trial funicular

steps.caption: left: extend the FIRST string and the LAST string (dashed) — right: the same two rays, o–0 and o–4, bracket the whole load line
steps.title: Close the funicular

steps.caption: left: the two extended strings meet at S. The whole system of four forces has the same effect as one force through S — that is what the funicular has found
steps.title: Their meeting point S

steps.caption: right: R closes the load line from its start to its end — left: the same vector through S, dashed green
steps.title: The resultant — in both diagrams

steps.caption: drag the pole o or the starting point: the trial funicular takes a completely different shape every time — and the resultant stays exactly where it is
steps.title: The answer

data.title: EX 1.2 — Resultant of several non-parallel forces
